recipes.name: The Best Thai Coconut Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 pound medium shrimp - peeled and deveined

steps.text: Heat oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add ginger, curry paste, and lemongrass; cook and stir in the hot oil for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in chicken broth, then stir in fish sauce and brown sugar; reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add coconut milk and mushrooms; cook and stir until mushrooms are soft, about 5 minutes.
Add shrimp; cook until no longer translucent, about 5 minutes. Stir in lime juice; season with salt and garnish with cilantro.

raw_recipe.headline: The Best Thai Coconut Soup
raw_recipe.description: This Thai coconut soup made with red curry paste, lemongrass, lime juice, shrimp, and fish sauce is full of authentic, bold, and tasty Thai flavors.

video.description: This one-pot soup recipe brings restaurant-quality flavor to your home without breaking the bank! In this video, Amanda shows you how to make the best Thai coconut soup on a budget. Featuring fresh shrimp, shiitake mushrooms, and creamy coconut flavor, this decadent soup will feed the entire family for cheap.

review.reviewBody:
I'm the one that submitted this recipe and I just wanted to add a little note: If you can't find lemongrass, most stores carry lemongrass paste. It's not as good as fresh lemongrass, but at least you will get some of the flavor. Also, I've discovered that adding basmati rice that is a little toasted or crispy adds another really great element to this soup. One more thing, my recipe calls for minced lemongrass because we like the texture and crunch of it. However, some people might not, so you can just put the whole stalks in a take them out when ready to eat. Thanks for all the great reviews!

EDIT: My recipe calls for 2 teaspoons of curry paste because I used incredibly spicy paste. Lately I am not able to find that particular brand and most red curry pastes on the market are not very spicy. So add to taste and according to how spicy the paste is that you have.

Holy smokes, this was AWESOME!!! My boyfriend snarfed it, and I loved it, too. My sister wasn't too hot about the chunks of lemongrass. I liked them, but if they bother you, you can always buy lemongrass paste, I suppose. Anyways, this was fast, easy, and total comfort food. Great recipe!

So good! I added a little curry powder and about a tsp. of lime zest. I was amazed to see the difference in brands of canned coconut milk. I picked up several cans of it on the aisle with the powdered and shelf life milk. Then I saw it in the chinese food section labeled Thai Coconut Milk and bought several there. Upon opening it was clear that they were different. The Thai product was creamy and thick on the top ( I have seen that referenced in other Thai recipes) The Thai product was clearly superior. Look for it. I will make this again. It was great without noodles or rice, very filling in and of itself for a meal for me.

I really loved this Thai comfort food. The second or third time I made it, I added some leftover lobster exoskeletons, including claws, to get every tidbit of flavor/meat extracted. Yummy!!! I did this at the chicken broth stage using the shrimp “shells” too. So it was a chicken/seafood broth which I found most tasty, and a good use for typically waste in Western countries.

Really delicious recipe! I sauteed a palm-sized amount of chopped ginger, a half tube of lemongrass paste, 1 crushed garlic clove, 2 tsp Maesri Thai Red Curry Paste. I then added 1 cup of chicken broth and let it all boil. I then added the 3 Tbs of Red Boat fish sauce, mushrooms, and 1Tbs coconut sugar, and another cup of broth. Let it boil and the ginger and garlic will dissolve. Then I added chopped colorful mini peppers, juice of an entire lime, 2 tsps of regular sugar, a tsp of white pepper, and the rest of the broth (2 cups). Then I added one can of regular fat coconut milk. I separately boiled rice noodles and then added them to the soup and added cilantro. Yum!!

To quote my husband, "This recipe is a keeper!" It is just as good as leftovers as it is fresh. I used 2 cups of chicken instead of shrimp and 1 Tbsp Lemon grass paste as our grocery store was out of lemon grass. Also as other reviewers suggested, I sautéd the mushrooms and used two cans of coconut milk instead of three. THIS SOUP IS DELICIOUS!

After reading the other reviews, I decided to use only one tablespoon of fish sauce, and 2 cans of coconut milk instead of 3. It came out AMAZING! I think that is a perfect ratio. I’ve tried dozens of recipes similar to this, and this was the closest I’ve found to authentic tasting Thai food! I also made it with veggie broth and tofu to make it vegetarian. I added some green beans and bell pepper. I’m super happy with this recipe, will make again!

Good base recipe! I had a few modifications. I didn't have lemongrass. I used 3-4 Tablespoons (not teaspoons) of red curry paste. 2 cans coconut milk (that's what I had). I used tallow from my farmer friend instead of grocery store oil. I felt like this combo was actually very good/delicious broth. I used minced jar ginger, very handy. I forgot the brown sugar and I didn't use any salt. I used Better Than Bouillon lower sodium chicken base for broth. I used a pound or more of large shrimp, thinly sliced red and yellow peppers, fresh green beans, scallions, & Bella mushrooms. Fish sauce, cilantro and lime as recommended. I served it over Basmati rice and I also made rice noodles. My husband loved it, he added hot sauce, always wants more heat! He said next time add more shrimp and also could add scallops or use fish in general. My step son, age 12, also liked it well enough and he suggested more noodles, and more shrimp. My first time making a Thai red curry based soup, and will make this again! I agree to add lime leaves and red chili as desired. I also would try peas next time but whatever you like.

Great recipe. As some have stated, I would use slightly less coconut milk. Two cans was perfect for me. Maybe slightly more curry paste. Also, take two to three stalks of lemongrass, whole, and let them simmer with the soup and remove before serving. I also subbed butter for the oil and added twice as much. Thai basil and jalapeno make great toppings in addition to the cilantro. Served with brown rice and you can't go wrong. Really great base recipe that you can tweak to your liking. Props to the original poster. Goes great with pork and beef as well.

Outstanding recipe, very family friendly. I omitted the fish sauce due to an allergy. I had chicken so I used that. I used 2 cans of light coconut milk to reduce the fat content. Add some sirracha to your own bowl if you want yours spicy. I seasoned with salt after. This recipe is definitely in my rotation now, thank you!

this soup is so delicious! it is full of flavors! the only thing i do is i put the chopped lemongrass in a small bag that i remove at the end because i do not really enjoy eating bits of the lemon grass. plus i added half of a spicy thai pepper it makes the soup even better!! this is the best thai soup!
I like to slice the shrimp in half so that it curls up when it cooks. I added 1Tbsp garlic in the first step.
Super tasty, easy to follow, and quick to come together. Will definitely make again!
I followed the exact recipe and I think it’s a keeper! Thanks for sharing!
One of the best coconut soups I've had--including from restaurants.
Wow. Easy recipe to follow. Nice to have a recipe for my favorite Thai soup. I have been making this soup with what I thought were the ingredients. Now I finally have the right recipe. Thank you.
I won first prize at the Soup-er Party 2025 with this recipe! It was sooooo good! Easy to make and I even substituted the mushrooms with just a can of sliced mushrooms. Yum! Loved it! Thank you!♥️
Excellent recipe! Use green curry paste if you want more kick!
My daughter and I thought this was just barely ok. Way too greasy, not creamy at all. The curry paste made it an unappetizing orange color. Will not be making this again.

So, I made this tonight with many alterations. Soup to me isn't soup without vegetables so I added celery, onions, a little carrot and a red bell pepper. I couldn't find red curry paste and had to use green which was just okay, and the lemon grass I bought was more like stalks. My biggest note here though is when you are making a fish soup use seafood stock, not chicken. I unfortunately used vegetable stock and it was the wrong stock. I will make this again, and will add the vegetables, seafood stock, and use red curry paste. I fought against my better judgement to just use essential oil for lemon grass and will do that if it's not fresh.
